question: Can a training-free post-hoc valid-time gate match a retriever that is itself adapted (fine-tuned or date-conditioned) to temporal context?
description: If a retriever fine-tuned or conditioned on temporal context outperforms a training-free post-hoc gate, the practical case for the plug-in layer weakens even if it remains convenient. No retrieved work compares post-hoc temporal enforcement against a retriever adapted to temporal context on the same query set, so the competitiveness of a training-free layer is unknown.
rationale: SituatedQA fine-tunes separate retriever and reader models per context type, and the legal review notes solutions are stronger at representation than at retrieval-time enforcement; if adaptation dominates, the plug-in framing must be justified on cost or portability rather than accuracy.
